item.text:
<linkedin_post>OpenAI is changing how ChatGPT responds when earlier conversations contain warning signs of possible violence. In those cases, it plans to make the model more cautious about sharing information that could be misused, even when a later question appears ordinary on its own.

The company is also working on a way for ChatGPT to end a conversation automatically when it shows signs that someone is fixating on violence or seriously harming another person. Multiple conversations ended for that reason could lead to a temporary account pause.

These measures depend on recognizing patterns across conversations and deciding when an intervention is appropriate. OpenAI says this work is ongoing, including efforts to recognize warning signs reliably. Its first Community Safety Report, planned for early 2027, is expected to include information on how its systems detect, investigate and respond to safety concerns.</linkedin_post>
